newsitem.title: USA: Metal Recovery eyes more zinc capacity.
newsitem.headline: Metal Recovery eyes more zinc capacity.

text.p: Metal Recovery Technologies, Inc said the addition of a third electrowinning cell by the end of April to its East Chicago dezincing plant will raise zinc and black scrap production to four to five tonnes per day and about 75,000 tonnes a year, respectively.
Earlier Wednesday Metal Recovery announced that zinc production will now rise to two tons a day due to the addition of a second electrowinning cell at the plant.
Metal Recovery processes galvanized scrap into black scrap and zinc.
Company chairman, Michael Lucas told Reuters that limited electrowinning capacity had caused a bottleneck, limiting the amount of scrap that could be processed.
Electrowinning removes zinc from the solution in which the galvanized scrap is treated. The plant, a world first using the patented process, started up last fall.

Meanwhile, Lucas said the company should be able to submit a detailed proposal to General Motors by August for a 100,000 to 250,000 tons per year dezincing plant to be built in the Michigan/Ohio region.
"All things being equal, we would look to be signing a contract in September," Lucas said. Construction would start by year-end.
The plant would recycle galvanized scrap for GM, return black scrap to the motormaker for remelting into steel, and sell the zinc.
"We would build it and GM would give a guaranteed supply of scrap," Lucas said.
